subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Crank: From Muscle Power to Rotation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Crank: From Muscle Power to Rotation.

hook.text: A hand crank converts your arm's back-and-forth motion into smooth circular rotation.

buildup.text: The crank arm acts as a lever. Longer arm means more torque at the shaft with less effort.

discovery.text: Medieval well cranks replaced rope pulling. One person could raise water that once took two.

twist.text: A bicycle pedal is a crank. Your legs push down and the crank turns that into wheel rotation.

climax.text: Cranks power car engines, sewing machines, and hand drills. Linear motion in, rotation out.

punchline.text: Push straight. Spin in circles. The crank bridges both worlds.

quiz.question: What does a crank mechanism convert?
options: Rotational energy into heat and sound
Linear or reciprocating motion into continuous rotation
